title: A — National Retail Lakehouse modernization
text: A retailer has three ERP systems, 14 regional stores, an on-premises SQL Server and a Lakehouse/Warehouse analytical estate. It is replacing manual nightly handoffs with observable orchestration. The business tolerates a 30-minute delivery window, but finance requires every posting to be reconciled.

title: A — Retail / least privilege
text: A retailer stores `Customers`, `Employees(Salary,SSN)`, `Products`, and `Sales(Region)` in a schema-enabled lakehouse. Business analysts must not see payroll data.

title: Analyst permissions
text: A user has Workspace Viewer access. They can query a permitted Delta table through T-SQL but cannot read Lakehouse Files using Spark notebooks. Operations assumes Fabric is malfunctioning.

title: Atlas text and platform rollout
text: Atlas receives text feedback, spreadsheets, and application extracts. The team provisions Lakehouses through automation and uses Spark for preparation. Preview functionality may be evaluated only in isolated pilots. Requirements differ between questions; apply the stated constraints rather than a universal tool preference.

title: B — Regional Healthcare Exchange
text: A healthcare data integration program shares parameters across master and child pipelines. Patient events arrive as customer-specific batches. The processing must preserve auditability, avoid exposing secrets and handle parallel facilities safely.

title: B — Regional logistics
text: A logistics platform has North, South, East, and West sales teams querying Delta tables across SQL, Spark and Power BI.

title: C — Healthcare compliance
text: A healthcare organization uses OneLake shortcuts, secured Delta tables, Power BI semantic models, and tightly controlled patient data.

title: C — Multiregion Logistics Telemetry
text: A national logistics operator ingests warehouse reports every morning and event-triggered files throughout the day. Missed runs, clock changes, and overlapping invocations affect downstream compliance reporting.

title: Case study · Alpine Analytics
text: Development and production use separate Fabric workspaces and separate connections. Dev's orders connection GUID is DEV-ID; production's is PROD-ID. The supported connection field is parameterized. A parent pipeline loads twelve unrelated entities concurrently; each has a distinct target table. A child pipeline accepts entity_name and target_table. A notebook requires batch_id in its parameter cell. Reports may refresh only after every entity load succeeds. Assume child calls wait for completion and all required access is granted.

title: Case study · Alpine Dimension Loader
text: A Fabric Warehouse contains one current version per existing CustomerId. A batch stages one canonical row per CustomerId after rejecting unresolved source conflicts. Region is tracked with SCD2; Email uses SCD1. Inputs carry a stable source change identity and effective UTC timestamp, both retained across retries. Unapplied genuine changes arrive in effective-time order, with timestamps later than the current version start; no retroactive effective changes occur. Changed rows and unique new surrogate keys are materialized before writes. Only one writer is allowed for this dimension. A Warehouse transaction can expire versions, insert replacements, and record the applied change identities atomically. An acknowledgement may be lost after commit. Reports require a complete valid version chain. No inferred member is present unless a question explicitly introduces one.

title: Case study · Alpine Equipment Monitoring
text: Readings has five rows: EventId e1, DeviceId D1, Version 1, Temperature 80; e1/D1/Version 2/Temperature 60; e2/D1/Version 1/Temperature 90; e3/D2/Version 1/Temperature 75; e3/D2/Version 2/Temperature 85. Version is a non-null source revision number; the greatest version is unique per EventId and corrects that event, not another event on the device. All rows share the same UTC day and arrive within retention. The report counts corrected events whose Temperature > 70, by the device's current region. DeviceRegistry has D1/RegistryVersion 1/West, D1/RegistryVersion 2/East, and D2/RegistryVersion 1/North. The greatest RegistryVersion is unique per DeviceId. Registry history must be resolved to one current row per device before joining. Both devices have a registry match. No other rows or policies modify results.

title: Case study · Contoso Finance
text: Orders are insert-only and OrderId strictly increases; no updates or deletes occur. A Warehouse control table stores last successful OrderId = 500. A stable new upper bound of 800 is captured. The target already contains IDs 1–500. Only rows with 500 < OrderId <= 800 belong to this batch. A separate target-side transaction can replace this exact interval and publish its control record atomically. No other writer modifies this interval. A retry may occur after an unknown commit outcome.

title: Case study · Contoso Web Operations
text: Visits contains unique VisitId rows, all timestamps in UTC. At 2026-05-04 09:00, three rows exist: A has VisitTime May 1 10:00 and ingestion_time May 1 10:01; B has VisitTime May 1 11:00 and ingestion_time May 3 08:00; C has VisitTime May 3 07:00 and ingestion_time May 3 07:01. The ingestion-time policy was enabled for all rows. At 09:00 an administrator creates two daily count views grouped by bin(VisitTime,1d): NewOnly with backfill=false, and RecentIngest with backfill=true and effectiveDateTime=May 2 00:00. RecentIngest uses async and succeeds. At 10:00, row D arrives with VisitTime May 1 12:00 and ingestion_time May 4 10:00. No other rows, duplicates, retention removals, or definition filters exist. Questions about results occur after D is queryable and backfill is complete.

title: Case study · Fabrikam Fleet Analytics
text: FleetTelemetry is ingested continuously into a KQL database. OneLake availability is enabled only for this table, with a 5-minute write-delay target. During a measured interval at 12:04 UTC, KQL exposes rows ingested through 12:04, while the Delta representation exposes rows only through 12:00. An incident monitor must reflect newly ingested records within 2 minutes; a separate historical analytics report accepts a 15-minute delay. Table retention is 30 days from ingestion; no archival process exists. Regional operators must see only their authorized region. Currently the table has no KQL row-level security policy; a request proposes adding one. The team must protect every granted access path, including direct OneLake reads, before releasing access.

title: Case study · Fabrikam Product Pricing
text: Product P8 has a SCD2 list-price dimension: SK 81 / price 50 / [January 1, March 1), SK 82 / price 60 / [March 1, June 1), SK 83 / price 70 / [June 1, infinity). Dates are in 2026 UTC. Actual sales are captured at order-line grain with Quantity and TransactionUnitPrice after discounts: February sale, 2 units at 45; July sale, 3 units at 65. Amount = Quantity * TransactionUnitPrice, in one currency with no tax or returns. A separate SCD3 summary keeps only CurrentPrice and PreviousPrice, initially 50 and NULL. The two subsequent price changes are applied in order. Product-name corrections must not change sale amounts.

title: Case study · Northstar Retail
text: A daily CSV is a complete inventory snapshot, including deletions. An immutable copy must be retained in Lakehouse Files. Analysts own a Power Query transformation that joins a supplier table and aggregates stock value by region. Reports must see a validated batch. File arrival is irregular. Identical events can be delivered twice, and an acknowledgement can be lost after data is committed. Business batch_id is stable across retries; pipeline RunId is different on a new run. Assume the necessary connectors and permissions are supported.

title: Case study · Northwind Regional Sales
text: Customer C7 has two complete, nonoverlapping versions: SK 71 / West / [2026-01-01, 2026-04-01), and SK 72 / East / [2026-04-01, infinity). Intervals use UTC and exclude their end instant. Orders arrive with natural CustomerId and event timestamp. Sale A: March 31, amount 100; Sale B: April 1 at 00:00, amount 200; Sale C: May 1, amount 300. Historical regional reporting uses the assignment at sale time; a separate report must restate all sales using today's region. A later email correction must apply to all versions without adding history. No other customer or sale exists.

title: Catalog governance
text: A consumer Lakehouse contains a shortcut under Files/data/dim_customer pointing to Delta storage. Spark reads the files successfully; analysts expect dim_customer to appear in endpoint Tables immediately.

title: Catalog validation
text: A mixed estate contains schema-enabled and legacy Lakehouses across workspaces. Resolution, data preservation, access enforcement and downstream behavior must be checked independently.

title: Cross-engine compliance
text: A hospital needs patient RLS enforced consistently for ordinary Viewer-level users reading from Spark notebooks, user-identity SQL endpoint and supported Direct Lake models.

title: D — Bank Regulatory Ingestion
text: A regulated bank receives files with multiple nesting levels plus relational lookup tables. It must detect missing files, monitor schema drift, observe freshness windows, and maintain a defensible audit trail.

title: D — Financial release pipeline
text: A bank promotes lakehouse definitions through Dev/Test/Prod with Git and deployment pipelines; identity membership differs between environments.

title: Data access governance
text: A team shares a Lakehouse item with a contractor using the basic Read permission but leaves optional Spark/OneLake data rights unchecked. The contractor needs to read Files via Spark for a training exercise.

title: Data platform deployment
text: A team uses T-SQL views for analysts and Spark views for notebooks. In production, a Spark consumer cannot query a view that exists only in the SQL endpoint.

title: Data platform regional expansion
text: An architect uses shortcuts to join producer Delta tables from multiple workspaces while enforcing OneLake restrictions. A query works in Spark but fails when issued to a delegated-identity SQL endpoint.

title: Data sovereignty review
text: A distributed team wants to join Delta tables from two workspaces in different regions through Fabric SQL analytics endpoint. Policy requires all source data to remain where it is.

title: Delegated SQL and OneLake
text: OneLake security roles limit region visibility in Spark. On the same lakehouse, a SQL endpoint in delegated identity mode returns more rows to an analyst than Spark does.

title: Delta platform modernization
text: One of the team’s legacy Delta tables uses deprecated multi-part checkpoints. They want to move to the new sync architecture without modifying the Delta structure.

title: Disappearing tables
text: A user says a newly created table is missing from the endpoint. The table was created in Spark using a location under a custom lake folder rather than managed Tables. The endpoint refresh was tried twice.

title: E — Manufacturing Spark ETL
text: An engineering team reads secured production telemetry using Spark 3.5 and writes governed gold tables for analytics.

title: Enterprise reference architecture
text: A fabric team has twenty lakehouses, three mirrored databases and one SQL database, all in the same tenant. Operations wants to know which ones require manual SQL analytics endpoint provisioning.

title: ERP modernization
text: A SQL developer insists that because the Lakehouse endpoint shares the Warehouse engine, all SQL Server statements should work identically. The team must validate migration risk.

title: ERP reporting SLA
text: A notebook publishes a new Delta table and a downstream SQL export starts immediately. Sometimes the export fails with “object not found,” but the Spark write succeeded.

title: ETL metadata changes
text: A schema migration adds two columns and drops a table. The lakehouse endpoint serves a large catalog, and the new sync architecture is enabled.

title: Executive KPI dashboards
text: A BI team wants to create a curated semantic model over the SQL endpoint, add DAX measures and relationships, and publish reports. They also use Delta table shortcuts to avoid copying customer dimensions.

title: Explicit prerequisite from V6-SEC-001
text: The contractor has Warehouse item Read, no workspace role, and only this SQL grant: GRANT SELECT ON hr.Employees (EmployeeID, Department) TO [contractor]; The table also has a Salary column.

title: External curated zone
text: Spark created an external Delta table in a non-managed OneLake location. Spark can query it by location, but the lakehouse SQL endpoint cannot see it.

title: External SQL tooling
text: A BI engineer is told to install a special Spark driver to execute T-SQL from SQL Server Management Studio against a lakehouse. The team has an endpoint connection string.

title: F — Central platform API automation
text: A platform team manages hundreds of security roles using the Fabric REST API and Microsoft Entra groups.

title: Fabric capacity monitoring
text: A new SQL metadata architecture advertises fresher catalogs. A team asks how to distinguish “Delta data changed” from “catalog metadata was refreshed,” and how to diagnose table-level sync blockage.

title: Financial restatements
text: Finance needs to reproduce a customer balance report from a prior UTC instant using the current lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint, without exporting a historical copy. The required Delta history remains available.

title: Fine-grained SQL operations
text: A recently created endpoint runs the new metadata sync. A dataflow overwrites rows inside an existing Delta table but does not add or drop columns. The team wants a targeted refresh without forcing all object metadata to reload.

title: G — BI migration and Direct Lake
text: A large retailer migrates Import models to Direct Lake and must keep row and column controls correct.

title: Greenfield migration
text: A workspace is configured with the new metadata sync preview. Two SQL endpoints were created last week; one will be created tomorrow. Administrators expect enabling the setting to upgrade all three.

title: H — Production incident response
text: A security operations team investigates reports of missing tables, blocked queries, stale permissions and inconsistent SQL results.

title: Healthcare data exchange
text: A data engineer must retain raw JSON for audits, transform it via Spark, and offer T-SQL reports. Data scientists also need to update Delta tables. The team wants to avoid a duplicate SQL data store.

title: Helios shared analytics
text: A producer Lakehouse on capacity P supplies a consumer Lakehouse on capacity C through internal shortcuts. Ordinary analysts have read-only access. SQL endpoint access mode is specified in each question; no assumption about its default is allowed. Both item access and data authorization must be satisfied.

title: Historical reporting portfolio
text: A reporting solution requires SQL endpoints for read-only analytics, Spark for ingestion, auditable as-of historical comparisons, and no duplicate storage. Operations also needs predictable visibility for new Delta tables.

title: Historical reporting with views
text: A reporting view was created on October 15. Auditors now request using SQL time travel against that view as of October 10, when its underlying Delta tables already existed.

title: Incident investigation
text: An endpoint created after enabling new metadata sync is missing a table change. Operators inspect the sync DMV: the table has an older latest_log_version and is_blocked=1.

title: Legacy endpoint incident
text: A Lakehouse SQL endpoint is idle for an extended period and then briefly lags behind recent Spark activity. The engineer sees a delay on the first reporting query.

title: Maintenance council
text: A retail platform keeps Delta order history for audit and serves analytical queries. Maintenance must preserve current business results, meet retention obligations and avoid breaking concurrent readers. Each question supplies the particular operating constraint.

title: Meridian supplier exchange
text: Meridian retains supplier CSV exports in ADLS. Suppliers may replace or delete files. A schema-enabled Lakehouse supplies SQL reports and Spark transformations. Raw evidence must remain available for audit. Preview features require an explicit pilot decision; no production approval is implied.

title: Migration board
text: An enterprise has development, test and production Lakehouses with notebooks, models and restricted readers. An interview describes a tenant-allowlisted migration; general production availability is not assumed. Each question states the evidence and required decision.

title: Mode-switch governance
text: Administrators plan to switch a heavily customized SQL analytics endpoint from delegated to user identity mode so OneLake filtering applies. The endpoint has SQL roles and functions that support reports.

title: Multi-workspace BI
text: Customer master data is curated in a trusted producer lakehouse. A consumer team wants to join it with local order Delta tables using T-SQL and avoid materializing another customer copy.

title: New sync adoption
text: Architecture leadership wants to roll out the new sync preview for a mixed workspace. Some endpoints are older; one table has deprecated multi-part checkpoints; another workspace uses private link.

title: Operations automation
text: A central pipeline processes dozens of lakehouses and must refresh SQL endpoint metadata only for endpoints with relevant changes. Operators want both ad hoc and programmed refresh.

title: Orion retail medallion
text: Orion has bronze.orders and bronze.products Delta tables in a schema-enabled Lakehouse. A silver MLV joins and cleans them; two gold MLVs aggregate sales. Daily BI tolerates minutes of latency. Unless a question says otherwise, SQL definitions are deterministic and source changes are inserts only.

title: Payroll analytics
text: The payroll lakehouse has a SQL analytics endpoint with SQL row-level security. A privileged engineer still has broad Lakehouse Spark access and sees all rows through a notebook.

title: Performance review
text: Engineering evaluates file layout and query latency using representative workloads. No speedup or percentage is assumed without controlled measurements.

title: Pipeline production cutover
text: A Lakehouse load finishes. The next activity publishes a semantic model report that references newly introduced SQL-visible columns. The team wants refresh to happen after loading, not before.

title: Retail BI platform
text: Retail transactions are written into Lakehouse sales Delta tables by PySpark jobs. The reporting team requests familiar T-SQL querying with no duplicate datasets.

title: Retention and audit
text: A Delta table was aggressively vacuumed, removing obsolete data files. The compliance team expects SQL time travel to reconstruct all previous table versions indefinitely.

title: Sales lakehouse schema migration
text: A team adds a column to a managed Delta table using Spark; SQL still shows the previous schema for a brief period. Business users propose creating a second SQL table with the missing column.

title: Secure enterprise workspace
text: A regulated Fabric workspace uses workspace private link. Architects want to activate the new metadata sync preview in that workspace while preserving private link.

title: Self-service finance reporting
text: Finance repeatedly joins sales.Customers and sales.Orders, and its reports need a reusable logical projection, not a persisted copy of customer totals.

title: Semantic model provisioning
text: An infrastructure-as-code team creates 40 new Lakehouses and expects 40 automatically provisioned default Power BI semantic models. They observe only the Lakehouse and associated SQL endpoints.

title: Sensitive payroll lakehouse
text: A tenant uses SQL endpoint RLS for reports. The same human is a Workspace Contributor, with broad access to local lakehouse Delta tables. Compliance expects the SQL RLS to constrain everything they can do in Spark.

title: Spark-to-SQL handoff
text: A data engineering pipeline creates a Delta table and then starts a report refresh. Engineers inserted a Wait activity of 15 seconds, but occasionally the report fails due to missing SQL metadata.

title: SQL performance triage
text: A query analyst proposes SELECT with joins, window functions, and aggregates. Another proposes using unsupported SQL Server-only features just because all queries begin with SELECT.

title: SQL review board
text: A reporting team has created a T-SQL view over sales.Orders and wants to make upstream Spark pipelines use the identical named object. They also use a Spark view in a different schema-enabled lakehouse.

title: Supply-chain SQL standardization
text: The team wants database objects for a read-only lakehouse serving analysts. Their backlog includes a SQL view, a scalar function, a SELECT-only stored procedure and a physical table with nightly UPDATEs.

title: Tax reporting automation
text: A tax service needs a stored procedure to return filtered aggregates from a lakehouse Delta table. Another requirement asks that the same procedure DELETE stale records.

title: Unified sales report
text: A query joins sales.Orders and sales.Customers. Audit needs a consistent historical as-of timestamp applied to both sources within a single supported T-SQL statement.

title: Vendor landing zone
text: A pipeline lands raw CSV under Lakehouse Files/vendor/orders.csv. Analysts immediately try SELECT FROM vendor.orders in the SQL analytics endpoint and find no table.
